name: Image resizer
title: Image Resizer: Resize Photos to Any Size, No Upload
description: Resize JPG, PNG and WebP images to exact pixels, a percentage or social media sizes. Batch resize in your browser; photos are never uploaded.
summary: Exact pixels, percentages or social media sizes, for one photo or fifty.
howTo: Choose your images, drop them on the page, or paste one with Ctrl+V. You can add up to 50 at once.
Pick a common size such as an Instagram post or a YouTube thumbnail, or type the width and height you need. Leave one empty to keep the proportions.
If the new shape differs from the photo, choose whether to crop, add borders or stretch.
Click a result to preview it, then download it, or download all of them as a ZIP.

faq.a: No. Resizing happens in your browser on your own device. Nothing is sent to a server, so it works with private photos and even offline once the page has loaded.

faq.q: Will resizing make my photo blurry?
faq.a: Making an image smaller keeps it sharp. Making it bigger than the original can only stretch the pixels that exist, so it looks soft. That's why “Don't enlarge smaller images” is on by default.

faq.q: What's the difference between crop, borders and stretch?
faq.a: Crop fills the exact size and trims the edges that don't fit. Borders keep the whole picture and fill the gaps with a color. Stretch fills the exact size by distorting the picture, which is rarely what you want for photos.

faq.q: Why is the photo's location data gone?
faq.a: The new image is drawn fresh, so hidden details such as the camera model and GPS location are not copied. That's usually a good thing before you share a picture.
